subject: Post-demo network readiness & SLO asks for private inference
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@novacare.ai>, tom.ruiz@novacare.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-11T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo network readiness & SLO asks for private inference

Hi Lisa / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our brief, I wanted to capture the specific networking and SLO items we discussed so your infra team can validate and we can scope a Private/VPC proof-of-value (PoV). Please see my notes below and confirm items you can share back (network traces, peering IPs, expected burst QPS, any existing VPN configs).

Key SLO targets (business asks):
- 90th percentile generation latency <= 60ms per token for 2k token sequences (streaming enabled).
- 99th percentile latency budget <= 180ms per token during steady-state (sustained load).
- Sustained throughput target: 600 tokens/sec aggregate across 12 concurrent sessions.
- Concurrency: support for 250 concurrent model sessions with 50 sustained QPS per session burst handling.

Network path & VPC items we need validated:
- Public egress path: are you using NAT gateways or egress via a firewall appliance (we need NAT IP ranges).
- VPN/peering topology: point-to-site or site-to-site? Any 3rd-party transit providers (Equinix/PacketFabric)?
- MTU: confirm if there are path MTU limitations < 1500 that could cause UDP fragmentation on streaming.
- Latency budget inside the VPC: please provide typical intra-region hop latencies to our colocated region (us-west-2).
- Packet loss / jitter expectations over peak windows.

Technical artifacts requested (if available):
- 1–2 minute pcap capturing a streaming session to our demo endpoint (UDP/TCP ports noted in demo).
- Current iptables/firewall rules affecting outbound to our IPs.
- Expected concurrency distribution (sessions vs sustained QPS).

Next steps / timeline:
- If you can share the pcap and egress IP ranges this week, Marissa and Karthik will review and confirm whether the targets are feasible without a fallback to Hosted.
- We can spin up a short PoV with a dedicated private tenant and synthetic traffic to validate latency within 48 hours of having the traces and IPs.

Attachments: demo-slide-deck.pdf (referenced during call) — happy to re-share the slides if helpful.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198

---
[Note: concise SLOs above to feed into engineering review — Michael]
From: Lisa Park <lisa@novacare.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@novacare.ai>, ops@novacare.ai
Date: 2028-05-12T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo network readiness & SLO asks for private inference

Michael —

Thanks for the clear summary. We discussed this with our network team this morning; high level responses below and we attached a short pcap from a 90-second test of a streaming session through our VPN.

Quick answers:
- Egress: traffic goes through a centralized NAT cluster (10.240.0.0/18 NAT pool egressed by a set of public IPs). Will send exact public IP list in a follow-up (need approval).
- Topology: site-to-site IPsec VPN to a partner colo, then direct peering to us-west-2 over a private interconnect (no cloud transit).
- MTU: our on-prem edges are set to 1420 for historical reasons; we've seen fragmentation on long UDP frames.
- Latency: typical infra-to-us-west-2 RTTs are 18–25ms, but we have spikes up to ~80ms during batch backups (occurs 02:00–04:00 local).
- Packet loss: average <0.1%  but we see microbursts during backups.

Attachments included: network-trace-20280511.pcap (pcap) — contains a short streaming session using the demo sample rate.

We can provide the public egress IPs under NDA; happy to do that once your team confirms they will only use them for PoV validation.

Lisa Park
Head of Infrastructure, NovaCare
lisa@novacare.ai
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lisa Park <lisa@novacare.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo network readiness & SLO asks for private inference

Lisa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the pcap. That MTU note is super-helpful — it explains a few of the demo hiccups. We will treat the public IP list as PoV-only and will not share externally.

Immediate plan:
- Marissa / Karthik will triage the pcap today to identify retransmits, packet-size distribution, and any clear causes for the stream-level jitter. Expect a short readout with recommended mitigations (MTU, keepalive, fragmentation avoidance) and whether we need to introduce a small client-side chunking or TCP-based fallback for streaming.
- If mitigations look straightforward (MTU + keepalive), we can proceed with a 48–72 hour PoV window using a dedicated Private tenant and synthetic traffic that mirrors your session characteristics.
- We will include a fallback policy in the PoV to automatically route to Hosted if in-region latency exceeds the 99th-percentile target for more than 30s.

Can you confirm who on your side will sign the PoV confidentiality addendum so we can receive the full egress IP list?

Thanks — will circle back with Marissa/Karthik's findings by EOD.

Michael
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-05-12T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo network readiness & SLO asks for private inference

Folks — forwarding Lisa's pcap and their notes. High-priority ask: can you review the attached pcap and answer the following by EOD?

1) Can we hit the SLO targets they requested (90p <= 60ms / token, 99p <= 180ms) if their MTU stays at 1420 and they have the observed microbursts? If not, what concrete mitigations do we recommend?

2) For streaming: would you prefer we recommend a client-side chunking change (smaller frames) or server-side fallback (TCP / chunk reassembly)? Pros/cons and estimated implementation effort.

3) Any additional PoV setup asks (IPs to allow, synthetic load profile — tokens/sec, session concurrency) you want me to request from NovaCare? We should be explicit so they can approve quickly.

Attachments forwarded: network-trace-20280511.pcap (pcap), slo-matrix-ask.xlsx (blank matrix with the targets above).

Thanks — Michael
